The '''2021 Census of the Czech Republic''' took place between 27 March and 9 April 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://english.radio.cz/national-census-take-place-despite-pandemic-8711920|title=National census to take place despite pandemic|date=2021-03-13|work=[[Radio Prague International]]|accessdate=2021-03-21}}</ref> It was conducted by the [[Czech Statistical Office]] at a cost estimated to be 2.23 billion [[Czech koruna]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://brnodaily.com/2020/08/13/news/2021-census-to-take-place-mostly-online-for-first-time/|title=2021 Census to Take Place Mostly Online For First Time|first=Veronica|last=Ugwu|work=Brno Daily|date=13 August 2020|access-date=7 March 2024}}</ref> Failure to complete the census could lead to a fine of 10,000 [[Czech koruna]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.e15.cz/domaci/nejen-volby-cesko-ceka-po-deseti-letech-scitani-lidu-1376628|title=Nejen volby. Česko čeká po deseti letech sčítání lidu|language=cs|date=2021-03-17|publisher=E15|accessdate=2021-03-21}}</ref>

==Preliminary results==
Preliminary results were released in January 2022. The national population was 10.52 million, which represented an increase of approximately 90,000 from the previous census in 2011. At the same time, the average age was reported at 42.7 years, an increase of 1.7 years in the last ten years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://english.radio.cz/preliminary-census-results-czech-population-grows-and-ages-8739116|title=Preliminary census results: Czech population grows and ages|first=Ruth|last=Fraňková|work=Radio Prague International|date=13 January 2022|access-date=7 March 2024}}</ref>
